planting.note: Direct sow in fall to allow natural cold stratification into moist to wet, acidic, sandy soil; established clumps die back to a hardy rootstock each winter.

directions: Florida Sunflower is a tall perennial of wet longleaf pine savannas, pocosin edges, and wet flatwoods along the Georgia-Florida-South Carolina coastal plain, distinct from the already-common swamp sunflower (Helianthus angustifolius) in its narrower native range and preference for consistently saturated, acidic sandy soils. From September into November it produces bright yellow, 3-inch daisy-like flowerheads atop sturdy 4-8 foot stems. Grow in full sun with reliably moist to wet soil; it tolerates occasional standing water during the growing season but should not be allowed to dry out for extended periods. A strong late-season nectar source for bees and butterflies, it is well suited to rain gardens, pond margins, and longleaf pine ecosystem restoration plantings.
sources: Flora of the Southeastern United States (FSUS)
